title: Why Saudi Arabia’s Last War in Yemen Turned Into a Quagmire
partialText: A Saudi-led coalition launched a military campaign against the Iran-backed Houthi militia in the country, reviving memories of its previous effort.

title: Wrongly Indicted Man Seeks Inquiry of Official Conduct in Reflecting Pool Case
partialText: Lawyers for the former Olympian David Hearn accused prosecutors of ignoring their own evidence to indict him and then providing “blatantly false” information about what they knew when.

title: Trump Does Not Plan to Reimburse Taxpayers for Promotional Ads
partialText: A day after the president said his super PAC would pay for the ads, which had drawn bipartisan backlash, officials said that he meant moving forward. A new taxpayer-funded ad aired Tuesday.

title: How Alaska’s Fish Became a Defining Issue for the Midterms
partialText: In the battle for an Alaska Senate seat and the governor’s mansion, the oil-dependent state’s declining fisheries loom large, but no one wants to look at the biggest culprit, climate change.

title: How to Destroy a Reputation in Hollywood, as Told in 5 Women’s Lawsuits
partialText: Five women have said they were the targets of malicious public relations campaigns that were spearheaded by three influential players.

title: Mixed Human Feelings After a Day at a Park Full of Robots
partialText: I went to Galaxy Robot Park in Seoul to see how we might one day live with robots. It was part cutting-edge technology, part theatrics.

title: France Student Protests Escalate Amid Fiscal Crisis and an Election
partialText: Chaos in schools, on the streets and in the markets is rooted in France’s struggles to fund its social welfare state, with a presidential election approaching.

title: US Solar Panel Makers Try to Catch China With a Big Leap in Technology
partialText: Manufacturers say they are close to perfecting a new, more efficient solar panel that could help the United States reclaim ground it lost.

title: U.S. Trade Deficit Hits 17-Month High Despite Trump’s Tariffs
partialText: Imports and the trade deficit have ballooned in recent months, defying the Trump administration’s efforts to reduce it through tariffs.

title: How Trump’s Tariff War With Canada Ensnared the Can-Am Spyder
partialText: The Can-Am Spyder has a devoted fan base across the United States. Now it’s a casualty in the trade war with Canada.

title: In Race With U.S., China Struggles to Recruit Foreign A.I. Researchers
partialText: China’s booming artificial intelligence sector has given local researchers good reason to remain in the country, but it has yet to lure overseas scientists despite a government push.

title: Secret Billionaires, Mafia Brides, Alpha Kings: The Insane World of Microdramas
partialText: Vertical soap operas for your phone have taken over film and TV production, and they may soon need no humans at all.

title: UK Security Adviser Jonathan Powell Traveled to Israel Ahead of Consulate Closure
partialText: Jonathan Powell, Britain’s national security adviser, visited Israel last week to try to negotiate over the looming closure of his country’s consulate in Jerusalem, according to three officials.

title: It Can Keep Cancer in Remission. Why Is No One Talking About It?
partialText: Despite mounting evidence that exercise programs can improve cancer outcomes, access to them remains limited.

title: As Spain Heads Into a Snap Election, Sánchez Turns an Eviction Into a Campaign Cause
partialText: The eviction of the woman in Madrid last month helped unravel Pedro Sánchez’s government. It also gave him an election platform.

title: Spain Cancels Arrest Warrant for Carles Puigdemont, Catalan Separatist Leader
partialText: The Spanish Supreme Court canceled an arrest warrant for Carles Puigdemont, who has been living in self-imposed exile in Belgium.

title: Two Arab Fighters for Democracy Have Lessons for America
partialText: Sitting on your hands is not an option when democracy is at stake.

title: The Science That Has Oil Companies Running Scared
partialText: However the U.S. Supreme Court rules, the work of holding oil companies accountable for climate change has a bright future.

title: Sally Yates to Lead Internal Investigation Into Cornell’s Handling of Sexual Assault Report
partialText: The university hired Sally Yates, a career federal prosecutor, to investigate how it handled a former student’s claim she was raped in 2024.
